title: The Fisherman and the Little Fish

keywords: the fisherman and the little fish
full_text:
An elderly fisherman sat upon a stone pier casting his line into the sea all morning without success. At noon, his cork bobbed under, and he pulled up a tiny sprat no bigger than his thumb.

As the fisherman prepared to toss the tiny catch into his willow basket, the little fish opened his mouth and gasped:

"Have pity, fisherman! Look at how small I am—I am barely a single bite for a hungry man! Throw me back into the cool ocean waves! Let me swim and grow fat for another season; then you may catch me again and sell me at the harbor market for a silver coin!"

The old fisherman slipped the little fish into his creel, secured the wicker lid, and replied with a serene smile:

"I should be a fool indeed to surrender a small fish already in my basket on the doubtful chance of catching a larger one in the stormy future!"
moral: A small certainty in hand is worth far more than a grand promise in the future.
